Tree exhibits significant lean accompanied by visible root plate upheaval, indicating potential root system instability and an increased risk of whole-tree failure.
Tree exhibits significant lean accompanied by visible root plate upheaval, indicating potential root system instability and an increased risk of whole-tree failure.

The tree exhibits a significantly asymmetric canopy, with the crown offset to one side and leaning over the driveway. This growth pattern creates a directional loading bias that may increase mechanical stress on the trunk and supporting root system.
Decay is present within the parent stem, compromising its structural integrity and potentially increasing the risk of stem failure.
The tree exhibits significant abnormal swelling at the root flare, indicating a substantial basal defect that may compromise the structural integrity of the trunk and root collar.

The tree exhibits greater than 40% canopy decline, indicating substantial foliage loss and reduced crown vitality. The central leader is also exhibiting dieback, further indicating significant decline in the tree’s overall health and vigor.
Significant soil erosion and deterioration of the root plate were observed, potentially compromising root system stability and the tree’s overall structural integrity.
A large fusiform canker was observed on the tree’s trunk at an approximate height of 30 feet above grade on the side of the tree facing the home.
